verdict.summary: There is no global, self-serve OAuth app that any Workday customer can click to connect: API clients live per account or per tenant, so each customer's Workday admin has to register a client (or allowlist yours) before their users can authorize. You can now prototype on a free-to-request personal development tenant, but distributing to many customers at scale goes through the Built on Workday producer program with Workday app approval.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Workday says a personal development tenant is usually ready within 15 minutes of the request, but the personal tenant is labelled beta and an earlier post described a waitlist, so access may take longer. Without a personal account you need a customer's tenant.

timeToProd.assumes: The common SaaS path where each customer's Workday admin registers an API client (authorization code grant) in their own tenant and gives you the credentials and endpoints; Built on Workday distribution adds partner onboarding and Workday app review on top.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Each customer's Workday security/integration admin to register the API client, pick functional-area scopes and grant domain permissions; for Built on Workday, Workday's app review and the partner order process.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: No source gives timings. The range reflects enterprise change-control for a per-tenant client and is our estimate; there is no single 'go live for everyone' moment.

verdict.cost: No fee is documented for a personal developer account. Built on Workday distribution runs through a Workday partner order process whose terms aren't public.

prerequisites.item: A Workday Developer Site account (personal email works for the developer program) or access to a customer tenant
prerequisites.why: API clients are created in the Developer Site console or in a tenant; Console tools need a Workday developer account.

prerequisites.item: A Workday administrator at each customer with Integration/Security admin rights
prerequisites.why: Per-tenant API clients are registered with the Register API Client task by a tenant administrator; Developer Site clients must be allowlisted on non-development tenants by a Company Administrator.

prerequisites.item: The customer's region-specific API gateway and authorization base URL plus tenant alias
prerequisites.why: Each account is tied to one region; calling another region's gateway can return 401.

prerequisites.item: Producer account membership (for Built on Workday distribution)
prerequisites.why: Built on Workday apps are distributed by a Producer, typically a Workday Partner, after Workday approval.

scopeTiers.impact: Development tenants are automatically authorized for all of your account's API clients. Sample data only (GMS staged company).

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Scopes in Workday are functional areas selected on the client, not OAuth scope strings you send.

scopeTiers.tier: HR read access in a customer tenant
scopeTiers.impact: No Workday review, but the customer's admin registers or allowlists the client and the authorizing user (or ISU) needs domain security permissions for every endpoint.

steps.title: Join the Workday developer program
steps.detail: Sign up at the Workday Developer Site with a personal email to get a Personal Account.

steps.title: Request a personal development tenant
steps.detail: Console > Tenants > Development Tenants > +. Workday emails sign-in details (usually within 15 minutes); sign in and change the password within 72 hours. The tenant expires after 7 days without login, and you can have only 1 active at a time.

steps.title: Create an API client
steps.detail: Console > API Clients > Create API Client: client name, HTTPS redirect URI, CORS domains if needed, and functional-area scopes. Save the client ID and secret.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Authorize at <auth base>/v1/authorize (e.g. https://auth.api.workday.com, or https://api.odp.wcp.workday.com/auth for personal accounts); POST to <auth base>/v1/token with an 'Authorization: ID <base64(client_id:client_secret)>' header. Map scopes by reading endpoint descriptions in the REST/Graph API explorers.

steps.title: Handle refresh and user-bound tokens
steps.detail: Exchange refresh tokens for a new access + refresh token pair. Access token lifetime follows the user's session timeout; refresh tokens die if the user is renamed or deactivated.

steps.title: Write the customer admin setup guide
steps.detail: Document for customer admins: run Register API Client (Authorization Code Grant, Bearer, your redirect URI, needed functional areas, optional non-expiring refresh tokens), grant domain security, then send you the client ID/secret, REST endpoint, authorization endpoint and tenant alias from View API Clients.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: This per-tenant flow is documented by integration vendors; Workday's own admin guide is behind its customer community.

steps.title: Build per-tenant credential storage
steps.detail: Store client credentials, region gateway, auth base URL and tenant alias per customer; your connect screen collects them before starting OAuth.

steps.title: Customer admin registers or allowlists the client
steps.detail: Either the customer registers a tenant API client, or (for a Developer Site client) their Company Administrator adds the target IMPL/SBOX/PROD tenant via Modify Authorized Tenants. Tenant refreshes from PROD can require re-consent.

steps.title: Optional: become a Built on Workday producer
steps.detail: Create the app with 'Create as a Built on Workday App', click Submit to Review, promote to Production after approval, then complete the partner order process.

steps.title: Workday app approval
steps.detail: Workday reviews and certifies the app; editing an app in Review sends it back to In Development. Approval expires after 1 year.

blockers.symptom: 401 Unauthorized calling the API gateway with a valid token
blockers.cause: The account is tied to a different region's API gateway.
blockers.fix: Use the gateway and auth base URL shown on your Developer Site profile (US, EU, SG, UK or ODP).

blockers.symptom: Client works in the development tenant but not in the customer's IMPL/SBOX/PROD tenant
blockers.cause: Non-development tenants aren't automatically authorized for API clients.
blockers.fix: Have the customer's Company Administrator add the tenant under Modify Authorized Tenants, or register a tenant-specific client.

blockers.symptom: Refresh suddenly fails for one customer
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens are tied to the user who authorized; renaming or deactivating that user invalidates them.
blockers.fix: Have customers authorize with a stable service account/ISU and re-authorize on failure.

blockers.cause: Missing or malformed client authentication; Workday uses 'Authorization: ID <base64>' rather than plain Basic.
blockers.fix: Base64-encode client_id:client_secret with no space and send 'ID ' plus the value.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: POST https://auth.api.workday.com/v1/token without credentials returned this 401 on 2026-10-20.

blockers.symptom: API returns permission errors for an endpoint despite a valid token
blockers.cause: The functional-area scope isn't enabled on the client, or the user lacks the domain security policy.
blockers.fix: Enable the scope listed in the endpoint description and have the admin grant the domain to the user/ISU.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error body is not documented.

blockers.cause: Personal Account tenants expire after 7 days without login.
blockers.fix: Log in at least weekly, or recreate it (data is lost).

nuances.text: Access token lifetime follows the session timeout the Workday admin configured for the user, so it varies per customer.
Tenant-registered clients can be set to issue non-expiring refresh tokens; integration vendors recommend enabling this for long-lived access.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: From Nango's guide, not Workday's public docs.

nuances.text: Scopes are Workday functional areas chosen on the client, and access is further limited by the user's domain security policies.
Service-to-service apps can use the client credentials grant mapped to an Integration System User (ISU), which avoids tying access to a person.
Workday recommends using only sample data, never PII, in WCP development tenants.
Workday's developer program now targets AI builders (Developer Agent, agent-ready MCP tools), so a Workday-hosted agent may be an alternative to an external OAuth connector.
